Replay

Browser identities and local checkpoints

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use Browser_Identity to retain a player's Session credential across browser launches. It reads or creates a persistent 16-byte Session token through IndexedDB. Keep it at a stable address, poll it before opening a runner, and obtain the token through browser_identity_token. A token is published only in Ready. Missing records are created with CAS(0); a competing creator reads the winning record. Malformed data and storage failures never produce a volatile replacement. Explicit test tokens can bypass this helper; they are not account authentication.

Browser_Checkpoint(S,C,A,E,N) owns a local self-contained authority archive and its observed storage revision. It uses the same canonical checkpoint codec as native save/resume. Open it before a new run or explicit resume:

Odin
storagegd.browser_identity_open(&identity, "my-game")
// On subsequent frames:
storagegd.browser_identity_frame(&identity)
token, ready := storagegd.browser_identity_token(&identity)
// Once ready, open one token-scoped slot with your model/content.
rgd.browser_checkpoint_open(&slot, "my-game", slot_key, model, content, token)
rgd.browser_checkpoint_frame(&slot)

Ready means the initial read completed. has_checkpoint distinguishes a missing slot from a validated archive. The loader checks the complete model/content contract and owning seat credential. This helper refuses permit-protected and custom-admission-policy archives: a local save is not a shortcut around Room approval. External asset dependencies need an application bundle, as Scrapyard already uses; they are not inferred from World.

During play, call browser_checkpoint_save(&slot, &session) on a local authority. The function captures the complete frame and session ledgers once and submits an asynchronous write. A true return means submitted, not saved. Keep pumping the game and browser_checkpoint_frame. receipt_serial advances after a completed write attempt; last_success, saved_tick, saved_hash and revision report the result. The saved hash includes the frame tick. Storage and codec failures are reported separately. At most one write is outstanding in a slot.

Writes use the slot's previously observed revision. They do not fetch a newer revision merely to enable replacement. A stale tab receives Conflict and retains the prior loaded archive; the stored winning archive is unchanged. Failed slots cannot write or resume until an explicit reopen/reload decision. An application can still permit a new unsaved run while clearly reporting that storage failed.

The checkpoint is owned by the slot. Borrow it only while Ready for a synchronous session_resume, which copies the required state into the new runtime. Resume still requires the owning token and a newer authority epoch. Do not destroy the borrowed checkpoint. Keep the supplied model and any immutable model.user data alive for the slot's lifetime.

Close with browser_checkpoint_close and browser_identity_close when their owner is released. Closing a pending write may discard a receipt after a commit has happened; it is not proof of rollback. Cavecrawl disables Leave while saving and reports success only after transaction completion. Browser termination can still interrupt a write, so reopening reads whichever revision actually committed.

These helpers inherit the browser store limits and durability boundary. Identity and save slots are separate transactions; a confirmed identity precedes session creation, so a completed save does not refer to an uncommitted new credential. Browser deletion/eviction and same-origin access still apply. There is no claim of portable power-loss durability or public identity provisioning.
